title: The cloud has
question: Where does the internet live, and what does it drink?
lede: Every reel you scroll lands in a building. India now has about 1,500 MW of them, most in a few water-short cities. Here is what they burn and drink.
words: A building full of servers that store and process what we do online.
Megawatts and gigawatts measure electrical power. 1 GW is 1,000 MW. Data centre size is quoted by the power it is built to draw.
When people and industry draw a high share of the water that nature renews each year in a region.

chapters.title: Four times, in five years.
chapters.text: Installed capacity rose from about 375 MW in 2020 to about 1,500 MW by 2025. Drawn to scale, the 2025 square is exactly four 2020 squares.
chapters.why: Why it matters. Private AI investment in India grew from $1.2 bn to $4.1 bn in a single year, and AI needs far more computing than ordinary apps.
chapters.src: MeitY, Digital India · World Bank, India Development Update 2026

chapters.title: Small for now. Nobody agrees what's next.
chapters.text: Data centres use about half a percent of India's electricity. A CEEW study expects 4.5 to 6.5 GW by 2030; the power ministry now projects an additional 26.3 GW of AI data centre load by FY 2032. Real trend solid, forecasts dashed.
chapters.why: How to read it. The two forecasts measure slightly different things, installed capacity and power demand, and still differ by four times or more. That gap is the uncertainty.
chapters.src: CEEW & SYSTEMIQ 2026 · Ministry of Power, Parliament reply, Jul 2026

chapters.title: One campus, one town.
chapters.text: Chips turn electricity into heat, and the cheapest way to remove heat is evaporating water. A 100 MW campus can use about 20 lakh litres a day. Divided by a city's planning norm of 135 litres per person, that is about 15,000 people.
chapters.why: Across India. About 150 billion litres in 2024, the daily water of about 3 million people every day of the year, expected to more than double by 2030.

chapters.title: Built where water is short.
chapters.text: More than half of India's data centres already sit in water-stressed regions. India has about 18% of the world's people and about 4% of its fresh water.
chapters.why: What could change. Closed-loop cooling, cooling at the chip and treated city wastewater all cut fresh water. Only 5 of 15 state data centre policies ask for sustainability today.
chapters.src: WRI India 2026 · S&P Global 2025 · Jal Shakti Ministry · CEEW & SYSTEMIQ 2026

takeaways: The internet is physical: India's data centre capacity grew four times between 2020 and 2025.
Power use is small today, and forecasts for the next decade differ by four times or more.
Water is the hidden cost: one large campus needs as much as a town of 15,000 people, mostly in water-short regions.

title: The gold
question: Why do Indian families keep their gold?
lede: Indians bought less gold by weight in 2025 and paid more for it than ever. Families rarely sell. More of them now borrow against it.
words: 1,000 kilograms. Gold demand is counted in tonnes; prices in rupees per 10 grams.
All the gold ever mined that still exists, in jewellery, bars, coins and vaults.
Borrowing money by pledging jewellery as security. The gold stays with the lender until the loan is repaid.

chapters.title: Less gold, more money.
chapters.text: Demand fell to 710.9 tonnes, down 11%. Its value rose 30% to ₹7.51 lakh crore. Jewellery fell 24% by weight and still set a spending record of $49 bn.
chapters.why: Why. Local gold prices rose 74% in 2025. Families paid more for less metal.
chapters.src: World Gold Council, Gold Demand Trends FY2025

chapters.title: Homes hold more than any central bank.
chapters.text: All the gold ever mined is about 222,600 tonnes. Estimates for Indian homes run from 25,000 to 34,600 tonnes, roughly one gram in every eight. The RBI holds 880.5.
chapters.why: Why we don't print one number. The "25,000 tonnes" quoted everywhere is a 2019 estimate built on a study from about 2017. The newer "34,600 tonnes" does not reconcile with its own valuation, which implies about 29,000.
chapters.src: World Gold Council · RBI · estimates in the ledger below

chapters.title: Families borrow against it. They rarely sell.
chapters.text: Bank loans against gold jewellery were reported at about ₹5.1 lakh crore in May 2026, roughly double a year earlier. Gold ETFs, funds that track the gold price, took ₹24,039 crore in a single month.
chapters.why: Checked, with care. The gold-loan figure comes from press reports of RBI data, so the ledger marks it "Check" until we confirm it in the RBI release. The government stopped new medium and long term deposits under the Gold Monetisation Scheme in March 2025, after it gathered about 31 tonnes.
chapters.src: RBI sectoral data, as reported · AMFI · Finance Ministry

takeaways: India bought 11% less gold by weight in 2025 but spent 30% more on it.
Indian homes hold far more gold than the RBI, though the exact amount is an estimate with a wide range.
Families are borrowing against gold and buying it as funds, rather than selling it.
ledger: ~31 t mobilised; medium and long term deposits stopped Mar 2025
